practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution defines the Gram Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243A provides for the Gram Sabha, which is a body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee first recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (appointed in 1957) first recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj system consisting of Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block), and Zilla Parishad (district).

practiceQuestions.q: Which Indian state was the first to establish Panchayati Raj?
practiceQuestions.sol: Rajasthan was the first state to establish Panchayati Raj. The scheme was inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on October 2, 1959, in Nagaur district.

practiceQuestions.q: Which amendment to the Constitution of India gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 added Part IX to the Constitution of India and gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 243B, which states are exempted from constituting Panchayats at the intermediate (block) level?
opts: States with a population not exceeding 10 lakhs
States with a population not exceeding 20 lakhs
States with a population not exceeding 50 lakhs
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243B(2) states that Panchayats at the intermediate level may not be constituted in any State having a population not exceeding twenty lakhs.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional duration (tenure) of a Panchayat under Article 243E?
opts: 5 years from the date of its first meeting
5 years from the date of election declaration
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243E states that every Panchayat, unless sooner dissolved under any law for the time being in force, shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting and no longer.

practiceQuestions.q: If a Panchayat is dissolved prematurely, elections to constitute the new Panchayat must be completed within:
opts: 6 months from the date of its dissolution
Before the end of the financial year
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243E(3) mandates that an election to constitute a Panchayat must be completed before the expiration of a period of six months from the date of its dissolution.

practiceQuestions.q: A Panchayat reconstituted after premature dissolution continues for:
opts: A fresh full term of 5 years
The remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued
A period determined by the Governor
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 243E(4), a Panchayat constituted upon the dissolution of a Panchayat before the expiration of its duration shall continue only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Constitution provides for the reservation of seats in Panchayats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243D provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in every Panchayat in proportion to their population.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the mandatory reservation percentage for women in Panchayats under Article 243D?
opts: Not less than 20% of the total seats
Not less than one-third (33%) of the total seats
Decided entirely by the State Legislature
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243D(3) states that not less than one-third of the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in every Panchayat shall be reserved for women (including seats reserved for SC/ST women).

practiceQuestions.q: Who determines the qualifications and disqualifications for membership of a Panchayat under Article 243F?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243F states that a person shall be disqualified if he is so disqualified by any law made by the Legislature of the State.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum age prescribed under the Constitution for contesting elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 243F(1)(a), no person shall be disqualified on the ground that he is less than twenty-five years of age, if he has attained the age of twenty-one years.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article deals with the constitution of the State Finance Commission to review the financial position of Panchayats?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243-I states that the Governor of a State shall, as soon as may be after the commencement of the 73rd Amendment, and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year, constitute a Finance Commission.

practiceQuestions.q: Who appoints the Chairman and members of the State Finance Commission?
opts: The Chief Minister of the State
The Speaker of the State Assembly
practiceQuestions.sol: The Governor of the State appoints the State Finance Commission under Article 243-I.

practiceQuestions.q: The power to conduct, supervise, and control elections to Panchayats is vested in:
opts: The State Ministry of Panchayati Raj
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 243K, the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to the Panchayats are vested in the State Election Commission.

practiceQuestions.q: How is the State Election Commissioner appointed?
opts: By the Governor of the State
By the Chief Justice of the State High Court
By a committee of MPs and MLAs
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 243K(1), the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q: The State Election Commissioner can be removed from office:
opts: By the Governor at his pleasure
By the State Legislature passing a resolution
Only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of a High Court
By the Chief Minister of the State
practiceQuestions.sol: According to the proviso to Article 243K(2), the State Election Commissioner shall not be removed from his office except in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of a High Court.

practiceQuestions.q: How many items (functional subjects) are listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution under Article 243G?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Eleventh Schedule (added by the 73rd Amendment) contains 29 functional items placed within the purview of Panchayats.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a compulsory (mandatory) provision of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
opts: Providing reservation of seats for backward classes (OBCs)
Organization of Gram Sabha in a village or group of villages
Giving representation to MPs and MLAs in the Panchayats
Devolution of powers and responsibilities listed in the 11th Schedule
practiceQuestions.sol: The organization of a Gram Sabha is a compulsory (mandatory) provision. The other options are voluntary (discretionary) provisions left to state legislatures.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a voluntary (discretionary) provision under the 73rd Amendment?
opts: Establishment of a three-tier system in states with over 20 lakh population
Direct elections to all seats in Panchayats at all levels
Granting financial autonomy to Panchayats to levy, collect, and appropriate taxes
Setting up a State Finance Commission every 5 years
practiceQuestions.sol: Authorizing Panchayats to levy, collect, and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls, and fees is a voluntary provision. The other options are compulsory constitutional mandates.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Constitution bars the courts from interfering in electoral matters of Panchayats (such as delimitation of constituencies)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243-O bars courts from questioning the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or allotment of seats to such constituencies.

practiceQuestions.q: Which part of the Constitution is related to Panchayats?
practiceQuestions.sol: Part IX of the Constitution contains provisions relating to Panchayats. Part IX-A relates to Municipalities, and Part IX-B relates to Co-operative Societies.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article in Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) mentions the organization of Village Panchayats?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) states that the State shall take steps to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to function as units of self-government.

practiceQuestions.q: The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA) was enacted in which year?
practiceQuestions.sol: PESA was enacted by Parliament in 1996 to extend the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to Scheduled Areas with certain modifications.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the PESA Act, 1996, the power to approve plans, programs, and projects for social and economic development before implementation lies with:
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the PESA Act, the Gram Sabha has the mandatory power to approve plans, programs, and projects for social and economic development before they are taken up by the Panchayat at the village level.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee was appointed to recommend the details of extending Part IX of the Constitution to Scheduled Areas, leading to the PESA Act?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Bhuria Committee (headed by Dilip Singh Bhuria) was appointed in 1994 to recommend provisions for Scheduled Areas, which led to the passage of the PESA Act in 1996.

practiceQuestions.q: In Scheduled Areas under PESA, whose recommendation is mandatory prior to granting prospecting licenses or mining leases for minor minerals?
opts: The Gram Sabha or Panchayats at the appropriate level
practiceQuestions.sol: Under PESA, the recommendation of the Gram Sabha or the Panchayats at the appropriate level is mandatory prior to the grant of prospecting licenses or mining leases for minor minerals in Scheduled Areas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following states is NOT covered under the PESA Act, 1996?
practiceQuestions.sol: PESA applies to 10 states having Scheduled Areas (Fifth Schedule): Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, and Rajasthan. Kerala has no Fifth Schedule areas.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the power to exempt certain areas or states from the application of Part IX under Article 243M?
opts: The President of India by order
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243M provides that Parliament may by law extend the provisions of Part IX to scheduled areas and tribal areas, subject to such exceptions and modifications as specified.

practiceQuestions.q: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a:
opts: Two-tier system consisting of Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat
practiceQuestions.sol: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two-tier system: Zilla Parishad at the district level and Mandal Panchayat consisting of a group of villages.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee first recommended that political parties should be allowed to contest Panchayat elections with their official symbols?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended that there should be official participation of political parties at all levels of Panchayat elections.

practiceQuestions.q: The G.V.K. Rao Committee was appointed by which body in 1985?
practiceQuestions.sol: The G.V.K. Rao Committee was appointed by the Planning Commission in 1985 to review the Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation Programmes.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee used the phrase 'grass without roots' to describe the bureaucratization of development administration at the expense of PRIs?
practiceQuestions.sol: The G.V.K. Rao Committee concluded that development administration had become bureaucratized and separated from local popular participation, rendering PRIs like 'grass without roots'.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee first recommended that Panchayati Raj Institutions should be constitutionally recognized, protected, and preserved?
practiceQuestions.sol: The L.M. Singhvi Committee (appointed in 1986 by the Rajiv Gandhi government) first recommended constitutional recognition for PRIs.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 243D, the office of Chairpersons in Panchayats at the village or any other level shall be reserved for SCs, STs, and women in such manner as:
opts: The President may by order direct
The State Legislature may by law provide
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243D(4) specifies that the reservation of offices of chairpersons shall be provided by the Legislature of a State by law.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article deals with the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats to enable them to function as institutions of self-government?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243G details the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats, including the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice.

practiceQuestions.q: The accounts of the Panchayats shall be audited in such manner as:
opts: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India directs
The State Legislature may by law provide
The Governor of the State directs
The Union Panchayati Raj Ministry specifies
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243J states that the Legislature of a State may by law make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Panchayats and the auditing of such accounts.

practiceQuestions.q: The Provisions of Part IX of the Constitution do NOT apply to which of the following states under Article 243M?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 243M(1), the provisions of Part IX do not apply to the states of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram (and hill areas of Manipur for which District Councils exist).

practiceQuestions.q: In which constitutional amendment was the reservation for SCs in Panchayats exempted for the state of Arunachal Pradesh?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 83rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 amended Article 243M to exempt Arunachal Pradesh from reserving seats for SCs because the state is inhabited entirely by indigenous tribal populations with no Scheduled Castes.

practiceQuestions.q: Who is eligible to vote in the election of the chairperson of an intermediate or district level Panchayat?
opts: Only the MLAs and MPs of the area
The directly elected members of the respective Panchayat tier
All registered voters of the Gram Sabhas in the district
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 243C(5)(b), the chairperson of a Panchayat at the intermediate level or district level shall be elected by, and from amongst, the elected members thereof.

practiceQuestions.q: The chairperson of a Panchayat at the village level (Gram Panchayat) is elected:
opts: Directly by the voters, or indirectly by members, as the State Legislature may by law provide
Always directly by the Gram Sabha
Always indirectly by the elected members of the Gram Panchayat
Appointed by the Block Development Officer
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243C(5)(a) states that the chairperson of a Panchayat at the village level shall be elected in such manner as the Legislature of a State may by law provide (allowing states to choose direct or indirect election).

practiceQuestions.q: Which article requires the State Finance Commission to make recommendations to the Governor regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the State and the Panchayats?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243-I details the SFC recommendations regarding tax distribution, grants-in-aid, and measures to improve Panchayat financial health.

practiceQuestions.q: Which body is responsible for incorporating measures to supplement the resources of the Panchayats in a State based on the recommendations of the State Finance Commission?
opts: The Finance Commission of India (Central Finance Commission)
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 280(3)(bb), the Central Finance Commission of India has the duty to recommend measures to supplement the Consolidated Fund of a State to assist the Panchayats based on the State Finance Commission's recommendations.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 243D, if a state decides to provide reservation for backward classes (OBCs) in Panchayats, it requires:
opts: A law passed by the State Legislature
A directive from the Election Commission of India
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243D(6) states that nothing in Part IX shall prevent the Legislature of a State from making any provision for reservation of seats or offices of chairpersons in favor of backward class of citizens.

practiceQuestions.q: Which schedule of the Constitution limits the legislative powers of states to override local self-governing rules in Scheduled Areas under PESA?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Fifth Schedule defines Scheduled Areas, and PESA (1996) acts as an extension act to protect tribal self-rule within these areas.

practiceQuestions.q: Under PESA, who has the power to manage minor water bodies in Scheduled Areas?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under PESA, the planning and management of minor water bodies in Scheduled Areas shall be entrusted to Panchayats at the appropriate level.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the PESA Act, 1996, the power to enforce prohibition or to regulate or restrict the sale and consumption of any intoxicant in Scheduled Areas belongs to:
opts: The Gram Sabha and the Panchayat
practiceQuestions.sol: Under PESA, the Gram Sabha and the Panchayat at the appropriate level are endowed with the power to enforce prohibition or to regulate or restrict the sale and consumption of any intoxicant.

practiceQuestions.q: The power of control over local plans and resources for Scheduled Areas under PESA is vested in:
practiceQuestions.sol: Under PESA, the Gram Sabha is endowed with the power of control over local plans and resources, safeguarding traditional tribal rights.

practiceQuestions.q: Who decides disputes regarding the election of Panchayats?
opts: An authority and in such manner as the State Legislature may by law provide
The High Court of the State directly
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 243-O(b), no election to any Panchayat shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as is provided for by or under any law made by the Legislature of the State.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article ensures that all laws relating to Panchayats in force immediately before the commencement of the 73rd Amendment continue until amended or expired (transition provision)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 243N provides for the continuance of existing laws and Panchayats, allowing a maximum of one year for states to bring their local laws into alignment with the 73rd Amendment.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:
1. It is mandatory for all states to set up a three-tier Panchayati Raj system.
2. States with a population of less than 20 lakhs are exempted from constituting Panchayats at the district level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (subject to exemptions). Statement 2 is incorrect because the exemption for states with population under 20 lakhs applies only to the intermediate (block) level, not the district level.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the devolution of financial powers to Panchayats, consider the following statements:
1. The State Finance Commission recommends the principles governing the grant-in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
2. The recommendations of the State Finance Commission are binding on the State Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Article 243-I outlines this duty. Statement 2 is incorrect because the recommendations are advisory in nature, and the state government must present the recommendations along with an explanatory memorandum of action taken before the legislature, but they are not legally binding.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Which of the following are compulsory provisions under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act?
1. Minimum age of 21 years for contesting elections.
2. Fixing the tenure of Panchayats at 5 years.
3. Direct elections to all seats at all levels of Panchayats.
4. Reservation of seats for Backward Classes (OBCs).
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are compulsory provisions. Statement 4 (reservation for OBCs) is a voluntary provision left to the discretion of the State Legislature.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the PESA Act, 1996:
1. It extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to both Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas.
2. In Scheduled Areas, the Gram Sabha has the ownership of minor forest produce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect. PESA extends Part IX only to the Fifth Schedule areas, not Sixth Schedule areas (which are governed by Autonomous District Councils under Part X). Statement 2 is correct: PESA grants Gram Sabhas ownership of minor forest produce.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the State Election Commission (SEC) under Article 243K, consider the following statements:
1. The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor of the State.
2. The conditions of service and tenure of office of the SEC cannot be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct under Article 243K, designed to preserve the independence of the local election administration.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended that the district collector should be the chairman of the Zilla Parishad.
2. The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended that the Zilla Parishad should be the executive body and made responsible for planning at the district level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee wanted Zilla Parishad as an advisory body with District Collector as chairman. Ashok Mehta Committee wanted Zilla Parishad as the main planning and executive body.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Which of the following committees recommended the constitutionalization of Panchayati Raj Institutions?
1. L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986)
2. Ashok Mehta Committee (1977)
3. Thungon Committee (1988)
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: The L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) and Thungon Committee (1988) explicitly recommended constitutional status for local bodies. The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) did not focus on constitutionalization as a primary recommendation.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gram Sabha:
Statement I: The Gram Sabha is a body consisting of all adults residing in a village.
Statement II: The powers and functions of the Gram Sabha at the village level are determined by state laws.
Which of the following is correct?
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct but Statement I is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement I is incorrect because the Gram Sabha consists only of persons *registered in the electoral rolls* of the village, not all adult residents (which could include non-voters). Statement II is correct under Article 243A.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Under the PESA Act, 1996, the Gram Sabha is endowed with which of the following powers?
1. Power to prevent alienation of land in the Scheduled Areas.
2. Power to control local plans and resources.
3. Power to manage minor minerals.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because Gram Sabha has the power of *prior consultation* before granting mining leases for minor minerals, but the planning and management of minor minerals is not vested in the Gram Sabha exclusively (it is handled by state guidelines).

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 83rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000:
1. It exempted Nagaland from the application of Part IX of the Constitution.
2. It exempted Arunachal Pradesh from providing reservation for Scheduled Castes in Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Nagaland was already exempted under Article 243M since the 73rd Amendment's commencement. Statement 2 is correct: it introduced the SC reservation exemption for Arunachal Pradesh due to its unique tribal demographic.
